paper_b.title: Simple Statistical Gradient-Following Algorithms for Connectionist Reinforcement Learning

pairs.why_related: A3C (Mnih et al. 2016) extends Williams's REINFORCE (1992) policy-gradient framework with a learned value-function critic (advantage baseline), $n$-step bootstrapping, asynchronous parallel actor-learners, and entropy regularization. Paper A explicitly cites paper B's REINFORCE and reuses its score-function gradient skeleton; the actor-critic + bootstrapping + asynchrony stack is the contribution of paper A. Paper B is PDF-fallback, so confidences are slightly downgraded where match relies on exact LaTeX rather than name/type.

paper_a.title: Adaptive Subgradient Methods for Online Learning and Stochastic Optimization

paper_b.title: Adaptive Bound Optimization for Online Convex Optimization

pairs.why_related: Parallel rediscovery of adaptive per-coordinate online learning. Duchi-Hazan-Singer's AdaGrad and McMahan-Streeter's FTPRL were developed concurrently (both 2010-2011) in different communities. Both derive nearly identical regret bounds of the form sum_i D_i sqrt(sum_t g_{t,i}^2) for diagonal adaptive regularization, and both formulate the same regularizer-selection optimization problem (trace-constrained quadratic). The papers differ in framing (mirror-descent / RDA vs FTRL with proximal regularization) and in the full-matrix treatment (AdaGrad does explicit G_T^{1/2}; FTPRL handles ellipsoids by black-box reduction).

paper_a.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

paper_b.title: Lecture 6.5 - RMSProp: Divide the Gradient by a Running Average

pairs.why_related: Adam (Kingma & Ba, 2015) extends RMSProp (Tieleman & Hinton, 2012) by adding a bias-corrected first-moment exponential moving average (momentum) on top of RMSProp's running mean of squared gradients. Setting $\beta_1 = 0$ in Adam recovers RMSProp's update up to bias correction. Adam additionally supplies an online-convex-optimization regret analysis that is entirely absent from the RMSProp lecture, and bundles AdaMax/temporal-averaging variants. Paper B is a PDF-fallback extraction (math fidelity reduced); names and types were weighted over LaTeX form.

paper_a.title: Mastering the Game of Go with Deep Neural Networks and Tree Search

The two papers thus instantiate the same conceptual programme — second-order momentum ODEs as a tool for analysing accelerated first-order methods — with Su-Boyd-Candes deepening it for the Nesterov branch.
